meta.face: A boy of about twelve of Roman southern Italy, visibly a child and not a young man, BEARDLESS, with a fair, rosy complexion and a LONG face that is FULLEST BELOW — a rather HIGH, narrow forehead, long, smooth cheeks widening to a BROAD, softly rounded jaw and a FULL, rounded chin; a LONG, straight nose with a rounded tip; LARGE, wide-open, clear BLUE eyes under faint, fair, high-arched brows; a very SMALL, closed, full-lipped mouth; bright GOLDEN-BLOND hair in thick, tight RINGLETS that stand out round the head and fall to the nape, the curly blond youth of his pictures; the gaze lifted heavenward, calm and unafraid. Not the round, dark-curled pancras, the square, dark cyril_caesarea, the heart-shaped, straight-haired agapetus, the wide, flat venantius_camerino or the narrow, freckled, straw-haired benezet; and not the round-faced, brown-eyed Christ Child of finding_temple with his soft golden-brown curls: Vitus's face is long and full-jawed, his eyes blue, his curls tight and bright blond.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; the face follows his pictures. Stracke (christianiconography.info): "customarily pictured as a youth with curly blond hair". Master Theodoric's fourteenth-century panel (Karlštejn, Chapel of the Holy Cross) gives him a long, full-jawed face, a long nose, a small mouth and thick golden curls, and the Master of Meßkirch's panel of 1535–40 (Karlsruhe) a curly blond youth with a palm, carrying a three-legged cauldron; the Golden Legend makes him twelve. The palm, the cauldron and the cock are his attributes (Wikipedia from the Catholic Encyclopedia; Ökumenisches Heiligenlexikon; Cahier's plate of 1867). The Roman Martyrology of 2004 names him alone, "In Lucania, sancti Viti, martyris".
